title: The Uncharted Summit
premise: Zephyrine Iversen, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Optimists—a cheerful, ruthless lending syndicate—takes one last job: escort a dying prospector named Halvard back to the mountains. In exchange for safe passage, Halvard trades her a hand-drawn map to the source of the Sorrowline River, a place officially erased from every survey because of what the government buried there decades ago. Pursued by both the Optimists' collectors and a survey officer, Wren Calloway, who is hunting the same map for reasons of her own, Zephyrine follows the river upstream through thawing passes and drowned valleys, slowly realizing Halvard's 'treasure' is a memory he needs returned before he dies. At the summit's forbidden source—an abandoned research station holding records of a disaster that claimed Zephyrine's own parents' expedition—she must choose between selling the proof to clear her debt and giving it to the mountain people who were never allowed to mourn. She chooses the mountain, burns her leverage, and finds that belonging was the only currency she ever needed.
about_author: Beatrix Thornbury is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons mapping tributaries in the northern ranges before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for landscapes that behave like characters and debts that behave like weather.

chapters.title: The Weight of Fair Weather
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Chasing a supercell across the flats to earn a fee that barely dents her debt, Zephyrine returns to find an Optimist collector waiting in her truck with a smile and a deadline: three weeks or collateral. The beat establishes her wit masking desperation.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Last Gas Station
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A coughing old prospector, Halvard, offers her a fortune to drive him into the high country before first snow. He won't say why, only that he's out of time. She refuses; then his offer doubles. Emotional beat: greed wrestling with instinct.

chapters.title: Terms of a Dying Man
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Over bad coffee, Halvard shows her a fragment of a map—the Sorrowline's headwaters, inked over official hatching marks. He promises payment enough to erase the debt. She signs on, telling herself it's just a job. Beat: the trap of hope.

chapters.title: The River That Runs Backward
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Driving upstream along the Sorrowline, they pass towns where no one will speak the river's name. A roadblock turns them back; Halvard knows a goat track instead. Beat: first hint the erasure is deliberate and enforced.

chapters.title: What the Collectors Drive
chapters.summary: Wren Calloway's POV. Introduced as a survey officer auditing permits, Wren is actually tracking rumors of the map—for the Optimists, who bought her silence years ago. She recognizes Zephyrine's truck. Beat: the hunter revealed as another captive.

chapters.title: Thaw Line
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The goat track collapses in a melt; the truck is lost. On foot now, Halvard weakens badly at altitude. Around the fire he hums a lullaby Zephyrine half-remembers from childhood. Beat: unease blooming into recognition.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They shelter with river-people living off-grid above the flood line, descendants of families displaced after 'the Incident.' An elder stares at Halvard like a ghost. Beat: warmth offered to strangers who shouldn't exist here.

chapters.title: Debts of the Cheerful Kind
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reports a false position to buy time, then interrogates a village contact too gently. Flashback: how the Optimists bought her after her father's failed expedition upriver. Beat: complicity and its slow corrosion.

chapters.title: Halvard's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Feverish, Halvard admits he was a station technician at the source when something went wrong—records sealed, valley flooded, blame assigned. He carries the only unredacted log. Beat: the treasure reframed as testimony.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Has a Name
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The elder confirms the lullaby belongs to the Iversen family—surveyors lost in the disaster. Zephyrine realizes Halvard knew her parents, and chose her deliberately. Beat: grief cracking open under the adventure.

chapters.title: Collectors at the Crossing
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The Optimists' collectors catch up at a rope bridge; Wren, sent ahead, must decide whether to signal them. She burns the signal flare into the river instead. Beat: love against duty—her first open betrayal.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. An early storm pins them in a snow cave for two days. Halvard fades; Zephyrine keeps him talking, piecing together the disaster in fragments. Beat: intimacy forged by shared cold and story.

chapters.title: The Map Is Not the Territory
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV (his only chapter). Dying clarity: the map isn't to gold but to the station's record vault—and to a grave. He recalls promising Zephyrine's mother he'd see the truth surfaced someday. Beat: tenderness, guilt, and purpose aligned.

chapters.title: The Pass the Government Closed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They cross the closed pass at night, past rusted signage and sensor tripwires Wren taught them to avoid via a note left in a cairn. Beat: uneasy alliance becoming trust.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Upstream
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Officially ordered to arrest them, Wren instead intercepts the collectors alone and stalls them with fabricated coordinates, knowing it ends her career. Beat: duty inverted; she chooses the people over the institution.

chapters.title: The Source of the Sorrowline
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. They reach the headwaters: a spring feeding an abandoned research station half-swallowed by ice. Halvard can walk no farther. He gives her the key and the last words of the lullaby. Beat: awe and dread at the threshold.

chapters.title: Everything Buried Was Documented
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Inside the vault she finds the unredacted log: the disaster was a containment failure covered up, her parents died trying to warn downstream villages, and the flooding was ordered. Beat: rage and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The collectors arrive with Wren at gunpoint; the lead Optimist offers to forgive everything for the log—it's worth millions in leverage. Halvard dies quietly during the negotiation, asking only that the truth go home. Beat: the choice crystallized.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren disarms her own employer's men; Zephyrine could still trade the log and be free. Instead she hands copies to the village elders and lets the collectors take only Halvard's body and her surrender. Beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Under arrest but unbowed, Zephyrine descends the river as the elders release the log publicly; the Optimists' leverage evaporates overnight and charges become politically impossible. Beat: the system buckling under daylight.

chapters.title: Names Restored
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Spring: a memorial at the source, her parents' names read aloud among the river-people. Wren arrives with her truck recovered and a job offer mapping the reopened valley. Beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Uncharted Summit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Standing at the spring with Wren, Zephyrine leaves Halvard's compass on the cairn and finally reads the whole lullaby aloud. Some summits aren't climbed but returned to. Beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
